scenes.tts: A kidney cell does not make synapses. Can one neuronal protein persuade an axon to build a terminal on it?
scenes.visual: Title card: What a Dish Can Show. A plain kidney cell in a dish with a growing axon nearby; a question mark.
scenes.narration: A kidney cell does not make synapses. Can one neuronal protein persuade an axon to build a terminal on it?

scenes.tts: Neurexin sits on the axon. Neuroligin is its partner on the dendrite.
scenes.visual: An axon terminal and a dendrite with neurexin and neuroligin clasped across the gap.
scenes.narration: Neurexin sits on the axon. Neuroligin is its partner on the dendrite.

scenes.tts: In two thousand, Peter Scheiffele and Tito Serafini's laboratory made kidney cells produce neuroligin.
scenes.caption: In 2000, Peter Scheiffele and Tito Serafini's laboratory made kidney cells produce neuroligin.
scenes.visual: Kidney cells turn a neuroligin colour. Credit: Scheiffele, Serafini and colleagues, 2000.
scenes.narration: In 2000, Peter Scheiffele and Tito Serafini's laboratory made kidney cells produce neuroligin.

scenes.tts: They grew these cells under axons from the pons.
scenes.visual: Axons from a pontine explant grow across a field of kidney cells, some with neuroligin, some plain.
scenes.narration: They grew these cells under axons from the pons.

scenes.tts: Where an axon crossed a neuroligin cell, synaptic vesicle proteins gathered into clusters.
scenes.visual: Bright puncta appear along the axon only where it crosses neuroligin cells.
scenes.narration: Where an axon crossed a neuroligin cell, synaptic vesicle proteins gathered into clusters.

scenes.tts: When the axons were depolarized, the clusters took up antibodies to the inside face of a vesicle protein. So vesicles were being released and retrieved.
scenes.visual: Antibodies against the inner face of synaptotagmin in the bath; after depolarization the clusters glow as the antibodies are taken up. Label: synaptotagmin antibody uptake. The Releases lamp lights.
scenes.narration: When the axons were depolarized, the clusters took up antibodies to the inside face of a vesicle protein. So vesicles were being released and retrieved.

scenes.tts: Control cells did not do this. Soluble beta neurexin, which binds neuroligin, blocked the effect.
scenes.caption: Control cells did not do this. Soluble beta-neurexin, which binds neuroligin, blocked the effect.
scenes.visual: Three parallel dishes: plain cells, no puncta; neuroligin cells, puncta; neuroligin cells grown with soluble neurexin, no puncta form.
scenes.narration: Control cells did not do this. Soluble beta-neurexin, which binds neuroligin, blocked the effect.

scenes.tts: The signal also runs the other way. Neurexin on a bare cell clusters postsynaptic proteins in dendrites.
scenes.visual: Reverse assay: a neurexin cell under a dendrite; postsynaptic proteins cluster at the contact. Credit: Craig laboratory, 2004.
scenes.narration: The signal also runs the other way. Neurexin on a bare cell clusters postsynaptic proteins in dendrites.

scenes.tts: So neuroligin is sufficient, under these conditions, to start a terminal on a bare cell.
scenes.visual: Label on screen: sufficient = adding it is enough to produce the effect, in a system otherwise ready.
scenes.narration: So neuroligin is sufficient, under these conditions, to start a terminal on a bare cell.

scenes.tts: But is it necessary?
scenes.visual: Second label: necessary = the effect does not happen without it.
scenes.narration: But is it necessary?

scenes.tts: Predict. Mice lack the alpha neurexins, or neuroligins one, two and three. Fewer synapses, normal ones, or synapses that are there but fail?
scenes.caption: Predict. Mice lack the alpha-neurexins, or neuroligins 1, 2 and 3. Fewer synapses, normal ones, or synapses that are there but fail?
scenes.visual: Prediction card with three choices: fewer synapses; normal synapses; synapses that are there but do not work.
scenes.narration: Predict. Mice lack the alpha-neurexins, or neuroligins 1, 2 and 3. Fewer synapses, normal ones, or synapses that are there but fail?

scenes.tts: You need two measurements. Count the synapses, and record what they do.
scenes.visual: Two tools appear: microscope for counting, recording pipette for function.
scenes.narration: You need two measurements. Count the synapses, and record what they do.

scenes.tts: In two thousand three, Markus Missler, Thomas Soodhoff and colleagues reported mice lacking all three alpha neurexins.
scenes.caption: In 2003, Markus Missler, Thomas Südhof and colleagues reported mice lacking all three alpha-neurexins.
scenes.visual: Genotype row 1: no alpha-neurexins. Credit: Missler, Südhof and colleagues, 2003.
scenes.narration: In 2003, Markus Missler, Thomas Südhof and colleagues reported mice lacking all three alpha-neurexins.

scenes.tts: Excitatory synapses were near normal in density. Inhibitory synapses were moderately fewer.
scenes.visual: Row 1, There column: excitatory near normal; inhibitory moderately fewer.
scenes.narration: Excitatory synapses were near normal in density. Inhibitory synapses were moderately fewer.

scenes.tts: And the synapses released transmitter poorly.
scenes.visual: Row 1, Releases column: poorly. The lamp dims.
scenes.narration: And the synapses released transmitter poorly.

scenes.tts: In two thousand six, mice lacking neuroligins one, two and three were reported. Brainstem synapses were normal in number.
scenes.caption: In 2006, mice lacking neuroligins 1, 2 and 3 were reported. Brainstem synapses were normal in number.
scenes.visual: Genotype row 2: no neuroligins 1 to 3, brainstem. There column: normal number.
scenes.narration: In 2006, mice lacking neuroligins 1, 2 and 3 were reported. Brainstem synapses were normal in number.

scenes.tts: But transmission was impaired, more so at inhibitory synapses.
scenes.visual: Row 2: transmission impaired, inhibitory most. A combined transmission lamp dims; Releases and Responds are marked not separated.
scenes.narration: But transmission was impaired, more so at inhibitory synapses.

scenes.tts: Add stargazer, from the first film. Counting found most synapses in place in every mouse. Recording found something wrong in every one.
scenes.visual: The full table with stargazer added, lamps set row by row. No alpha-neurexins: There mostly lit (inhibitory fewer), Releases dim. No neuroligins 1 to 3: There lit, transmission dim, with release and response marked not separated. Stargazer: There lit, Releases lit, Responds split, NMDA lit and AMPA dark.
scenes.narration: Add stargazer, from the first film. Counting found most synapses in place in every mouse. Recording found something wrong in every one.

scenes.tts: This does not mean deletions never change number. Deleting every neurexin from some interneurons does lower synapse number.
scenes.visual: Small side note on screen: some interneurons, all neurexins deleted: fewer synapses.
scenes.narration: This does not mean deletions never change number. Deleting every neurexin from some interneurons does lower synapse number.

scenes.tts: Why would the brain manage without it?
scenes.visual: Question card.
scenes.narration: Why would the brain manage without it?

scenes.tts: One likely reason is overlap. Several organizers can start contacts, so removing one family leaves others.
scenes.visual: Several organizer pairs bridge the cleft; one pair is removed and the others still hold.
scenes.narration: One likely reason is overlap. Several organizers can start contacts, so removing one family leaves others.

scenes.tts: Another is that some organizers specify or check contacts, rather than start them.
scenes.visual: A contact forms; an organizer tags it as excitatory or inhibitory and keeps it.
scenes.narration: Another is that some organizers specify or check contacts, rather than start them.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: a dish tests what one protein can start. A mouse tests what the brain cannot do without. Measure function, as well as count.
scenes.visual: Closing card: dish = what it can start; mouse = what the brain needs.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: a dish tests what one protein can start. A mouse tests what the brain cannot do without. Measure function, as well as count.
